newsitem.title: ITALY: U.S. says there is no automatic right to food.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says there is no automatic right to food.

text.p: The United States said in Sunday that achieving the right to adequate food was "a goal or aspiration" and not an international obligation on governments.

In a written reservation to a declaration on hunger adopted at a U.N.-sponsored World Food Summit, Washington also said it had not signed up to a summit target that countries should provide 0.7 percent of their annual economic wealth in overseas development aid.

The five-day summit, which ends on Sunday, adopted by consensus at its outset a document which reaffirms "the right of everyone to have access to safe and nutritious food consistent with the right to adequate food and the fundamental right of everyone to be free from hunger".

"The United States believes that (this) is a goal or aspiration to be realised progressively but does not give rise to any international obligations nor diminish the responsibility of national governments towards their citizens," the U.S. reservation said.
It was among written reservations or interpretations to the summit document lodged by 15 countries, organisers said.
Others, including the Vatican, Argentina and several Moslem states raised strong objections to references in the summit texts to population and family planning policies.
